dialog.card.copiedRef.context: Toast after Copy Reference. {ref} is the card's own reference.

dialog.block.reasonPrompt.context: Prompt of the input box Block raises before it runs dinah block.

dialog.move.noLegalMoves.text: {ref} has no legal moves from where it stands.
dialog.move.noLegalMoves.context: Shown when instructions answered with an empty legal-move list. {ref} is the card's reference.

dialog.move.placeholder.context: Placeholder of the quick pick listing a card's legal destinations. {ref} is the card's reference.

dialog.move.backward.context: The detail line marking a destination that lies behind the card's current column.

dialog.openOutput.label.context: The button a warning toast offers when the Dinah output channel holds the detail.

dialog.column.instructionsUnreadable.cha.text: {column}: could not open this column's instructions file. {detail}
dialog.column.instructionsUnreadable.cha.context: Output channel line when Edit Instructions could not resolve the file. {column} is the row's label, {detail} the refusal.

dialog.column.instructionsUnreadable.toa.text: {column}: could not open this column's instructions file. See the Dinah output channel for details.
dialog.column.instructionsUnreadable.toa.context: Toast beside the channel line above, pointing at the channel. {column} is the row's label.

dialog.workbench.noReport.channel.text: {workbench}: check produced no report the extension could read. {detail}
dialog.workbench.noReport.channel.context: Output channel line when check answered with no report this build could read. {workbench} is the row's label, {detail} the refusal.

dialog.workbench.noReport.toast.text: {workbench}: check produced no report the extension could read. See the Dinah output channel for details.
dialog.workbench.noReport.toast.context: Toast beside the channel line above, pointing at the channel. {workbench} is the row's label.

dialog.workbench.noBinary.text: No dinah binary was resolved, so nothing ran.
dialog.workbench.noBinary.context: Channel line naming the binary that answered, when no binary was resolved at all.

dialog.workbench.answeringBinary.context: Channel line naming the binary that answered. {exe} is its path.

dialog.workbench.answeringBinaryDescribe.context: As above, with the binary's self-reported version. {exe} is the path, {description} the version line.

dialog.workbench.checkClean.context: Toast after a check that found nothing. {workbench} is the row's label.

dialog.workbench.checkFindings.channel.context: Heading above the findings in the output channel. {workbench} is the row's label, {count} the number of findings.

dialog.workbench.checkFindings.toast.text: {workbench}: check found {count} defect(s). See the Dinah output channel for details.
dialog.workbench.checkFindings.toast.context: Toast beside the heading above, pointing at the channel. {workbench} is the row's label, {count} the number of findings.

dialog.workbench.copiedPath.context: Toast after Copy Path. {path} is the workbench's own directory.

dialog.workbench.definitionUnreadable.ch.text: {workbench}: could not open the workbench definition file. {detail}
dialog.workbench.definitionUnreadable.ch.context: Output channel line when Edit Definition could not resolve the file. {workbench} is the row's label, {detail} the refusal.

dialog.workbench.definitionUnreadable.to.text: {workbench}: could not open the workbench definition file. See the Dinah output channel for details.
dialog.workbench.definitionUnreadable.to.context: Toast beside the channel line above, pointing at the channel. {workbench} is the row's label.

dialog.newCard.titlePrompt.text: Title for the new card in {column}
dialog.newCard.titlePrompt.context: Prompt of the input box New Card raises. {column} is the row's label.

dialog.attach.descriptionPrompt.text: Description for this attachment, or leave blank
dialog.attach.descriptionPrompt.context: Prompt of the input box Attach File raises after the file has been chosen.

dialog.pull.empty.text: Nothing in {from} is ready to pull into {into}.
dialog.pull.empty.context: Toast after a pull that was allowed and found nothing. {from} is the upstream's title, {into} the destination's.

dialog.drop.crossWorkbench.text: Dinah cannot move {ref} into {destination}, because that column belongs to a different workbench.
dialog.drop.crossWorkbench.context: Shown when a card is dragged onto a column of another workbench. {ref} is the card, {destination} the column.

dialog.drop.thatColumn.context: Stands in for the destination in the message above when the drop resolved no column at all.

tree.column.damaged.context: The description on the column row the last read named as unreadable.

tree.column.brokenTooltip.unreadable.text: This column's own file could not be read.
tree.column.brokenTooltip.unreadable.context: The hover line saying why the column row carries a warning marker.

tree.column.occupancyWaiting.context: A column row's description when the column waits on somebody outside. {occupancy} is the count, or the count over the capacity.

tree.column.claimedHere.context: Hover line on a column that takes work up.

tree.column.pulledOnward.text: A card here waits to be pulled onward.
tree.column.pulledOnward.context: Hover line on a queue column, which holds a card rather than taking work up.

tree.column.pullHint.text: Right-click to pull the next ready card into {destination}.
tree.column.pullHint.context: Hover line telling the reader where the row's Pull would land the card. {destination} is the next column's title.

tree.column.awaitingOutside.text: This column is waiting on somebody outside the workbench.
tree.column.awaitingOutside.context: Hover line on a column whose cards wait on somebody outside the workbench.

tree.column.operatorOwned.text: Only the operator moves a card out.
tree.column.operatorOwned.context: Hover line on a column only the operator moves a card out of.

tree.column.agentMoves.text: An agent moves a card out.
tree.column.agentMoves.context: Hover line on a column an agent moves a card out of.

tree.card.heldBy.context: Hover line on an active card. {holder} is the actor holding it.

tree.group.ready.context: The heading over the ready cards standing at a column.

tree.group.active.context: The heading over the active cards standing at a column.

tree.group.blocked.context: The heading over the blocked cards standing at a column.

tree.group.none.context: The heading over a group whose axis value the read left empty.

tree.attachments.label.context: The row heading the files attached to a card.

tree.attachment.noLocalFile.context: The last hover line on an attachment row whose payload is not on this machine.

tree.root.noWorkbench.context: Stands in for the refusal on a folder row where the walk found nothing and said nothing.

tree.root.deadEnd.noWorkbenchSentence.text: No workbench was found from this folder. Run `dinah init` in a terminal to create one, or set `dinah.workbench` to the directory of one you already have.
tree.root.deadEnd.noWorkbenchSentence.context: The hover on a folder row the walk found no workbench under, when the walk said so rather than refusing.

tree.root.deadEnd.label.context: The label of a folder row the walk found no workbench under. {folder} is the folder's name, {refusal} what the walk said. Two placeholders and a separator, with no word to translate.

tree.root.unreadable.tooltip.text: The walk could not read this directory: {refusal}
tree.root.unreadable.tooltip.context: The hover on a row the walk could not read far enough to name. {refusal} is what it said.

tree.root.wouldNotOpen.context: A workbench row's description when the workbench refused to open at all.

tree.root.didNotAnswer.context: A workbench row's description when the workbench opened and declined one question.

status.noBinary.notFound.text: No dinah binary was found. This extension is a companion to the dinah command-line tool and carries no copy of it.
status.noBinary.notFound.context: First hover line on the status bar item when no dinah binary was found.

status.noBinary.install.text: Install it from https://github.com/paulmooreparks/dinah#install, or set dinah.path to a binary you already have.
status.noBinary.install.context: Second hover line on the status bar item when no dinah binary was found.

status.ambiguous.text: Several workbenches are reachable from here. Set dinah.workbench to choose one.
status.ambiguous.context: Hover line on the status bar item when several workbenches are reachable.

status.refused.context: Hover line carrying a refusal the resolution answered with. {refusal} is the refusal's own name.

status.binary.withSource.context: Hover line naming the binary this window drives. {path} is its path, {source} where it was found.

status.binary.plain.context: As above, when the source is not known. {path} is the binary's path.

status.pairedWith.context: Hover line naming the dinah release this build of the extension was cut alongside. {release} is that tag.

status.resolvedBy.context: Hover line saying how the workbench was found. {source} is the resolution's own source.

status.outsideWorkspace.text: This workbench is outside your workspace: {root}
status.outsideWorkspace.context: Leading hover line when the walk climbed past the workspace folder. {root} is the workbench's directory.

status.holding.remaining.hours.context: Time left on a claim of an hour or more, shown beside the card's reference in the status bar. {hours} is whole hours, {minutes} the minutes after them.

status.holding.remaining.minutes.context: Time left on a claim of under an hour, shown beside the card's reference in the status bar. {minutes} is whole minutes.

status.holding.remaining.soon.context: Time left on a claim that lapses within the minute, shown beside the card's reference in the status bar.

status.holding.remaining.expired.context: Shown in place of a time when the claim's lease has already lapsed.

status.holding.remaining.noLease.context: Shown in place of a time when the claim carries no lease and so never lapses.

status.holding.tooltipLead.context: First hover line when the reader holds exactly one card. {ref} is the card's reference, {workbench} the workbench's title, {clause} one of the five remaining-time clauses.

status.holding.tooltipLeadMany.context: First hover line when the reader holds more than one card. {count} is how many, and {ref}, {workbench} and {clause} describe the one whose lease lapses first.

status.holding.tooltipRow.context: One hover line per further held card, under the lead line. {ref} is the card's reference, {workbench} the workbench's title, {clause} its remaining-time clause. Two references, a separator and a clause, so a language whose preposition here is also "in" renders it identically.

status.holding.uncertainLead.text: Dinah could not confirm whether you are holding anything right now
status.holding.uncertainLead.context: First hover line when every workbench's last read went stale, so the window cannot say what the reader holds.

servedText.title.instructions.context: Tab label of the editor tab a card's served instruction chain opens in. {ref} is the card's own reference.

servedText.heading.global.context: Markdown heading above the user-global layer of a served instruction chain.

servedText.heading.standing.context: Markdown heading above the workbench's own standing layer of a served instruction chain.

servedText.heading.column.context: Markdown heading above the column's own layer of a served instruction chain.

servedText.malformedUri.text: This served-text tab's own URI could not be read.
servedText.malformedUri.context: Body of a served-text tab whose URI carries no kind, no workbench or no reference.

servedText.unknownKind.text: Dinah has no way to show text of kind {kind}.
servedText.unknownKind.context: Body of a served-text tab naming a kind of text this extension serves no reader for. {kind} is that name.

servedText.refused.context: Body of a served-text tab whose fetch was refused. {detail} is what dinah said.

servedText.title.guide.context: Tab title for a live-fetched guide, opened today only from the first-session walkthrough. {topic} is the guide's own topic slug (e.g. first-session) and is not translated.

servedText.title.history.context: Tab label of the editor tab a card's own journal opens in. {ref} is the card's own reference.

history.empty.text: No history is recorded for this card.
history.empty.context: Body of the history tab when the journal read succeeded and returned no events at all.

history.value.none.context: Stands in for an absent from or to value on a history row reporting a change to one of a card's own fields.

history.event.created.context: History row for a card's creation. {actor} is who acted, {title} the card's title, {toTitle} the title of the column it was filed into.

history.event.claimed.context: History row for a claim. {actor} is who claimed it.

history.event.moved.context: History row for a move. {fromTitle} and {toTitle} are the two columns' titles as of the move.

history.event.released.context: History row for a release. {actor} is who let the card go.

history.event.blocked.context: History row for a block. {reason} is the prose reason the block carried, which is never empty.

history.event.unblocked.context: History row for an unblock. {actor} is who lifted the block.

history.event.expired.context: History row for a claim that lapsed. {actor} is the holder whose claim ran out.

history.event.commented.context: History row for a comment. The comment's own text is not in the journal, so the row names only who wrote one.

history.event.attached.context: History row for an attachment being added. {filename} is the file's name as of the event.

history.event.attachment_replaced.context: History row for an attachment's contents being replaced. {filename} is the new file's name.

history.event.attachment_removed.context: History row for an attachment being removed. {filename} is the name it carried when it went.

history.event.attachment_renamed.context: History row for an attachment being renamed. {from} is the old filename and {filename} the new one.

history.event.archived.context: History row for an archive. The row does not name what was archived, because the event carries a bare identifier that cannot say whether it names the card or one of its attachments, and a reader reaches this tab from a live card row, so an attachment is the usual answer. The wording follows history.event.deleted, which carries the same ambiguity.

history.event.restored.context: History row for a restore. No command writes this event today, and the row exists so that a binary which starts writing one needs no change here. The wording follows history.event.deleted, which carries the same ambiguity about what was acted on.

history.event.deleted.context: History row for a deletion. Nothing writes this event onto a card's own journal today, and the row exists for the same forward-compatibility reason the restore row does.

history.event.manual_correction.text: {actor} corrected the card's recorded position from {fromTitle} to {toTitle}.
history.event.manual_correction.context: History row for a witnessed correction. {fromTitle} and {toTitle} are the believed and the anchored column at the moment the drift was witnessed.

history.event.workstream_joined.context: History row for a workstream membership being taken up. {workstream} is the raw identifier, since the event captures no title for it.

history.event.workstream_left.context: History row for a workstream membership being given up. {workstream} is the raw identifier, since the event captures no title for it.

history.event.card_updated.context: History row for a write to one of a card's own fields. {field} is the field's name, and {from} and {to} carry its value on either side of the write, each filled with the catalogue's word for an absent value when the event carries none.

history.event.tier_overridden.text: {actor} set the card's tier in {columnTitle} to {to} ({expr}).
history.event.tier_overridden.context: History row for a per-card tier override being written for one column. The sentence names the card because the override belongs to the card and not to the column. {columnTitle} is the column's title as of the event and falls back to its raw identifier when the event captured none, {to} is the resolved value and {expr} is what somebody typed.

history.event.tier_override_dropped.text: {actor}'s tier override for the card in {column} ({from}) was dropped because the column was retired.
history.event.tier_override_dropped.context: History row for a per-card tier override dropped when the column it applied in was retired by a reshape. {column} is that column's raw identifier and {from} the value that went with it.

history.event.unknown.context: History row for an event name this catalogue does not recognise, which is what a newer binary's event renders as. {event} is that raw name and is not translated.

diagnostics.check.uncertain.text: {workbench}: check has not completed, so whether it is clean is not known.
diagnostics.check.uncertain.context: Placeholder diagnostic shown on a workbench's own definition file until the first `dinah check` run of the session for that workbench answers, so an empty Problems panel never means both "confirmed clean" and "never checked, or check failed."

dialog.runVerb.pickVerbPlaceholder.context: Placeholder of the quick pick listing every verb this build can render, opened by the Run Command entry.

dialog.runVerb.excludedSeparator.text: {count} command(s) not shown; see the Dinah output channel for why.
dialog.runVerb.excludedSeparator.context: Label of the trailing separator row in the verb quick pick when one or more served tools were left out as unrenderable. {count} is how many.

dialog.runVerb.requiredValuePrompt.context: Prompt of the input box for a required string argument of the chosen verb. {argument} is the argument's own untranslated name, and an empty or whitespace-only answer reopens this same prompt.

dialog.runVerb.optionalValuePrompt.context: Prompt of the input box for an optional string argument. A blank answer leaves the argument out of the call rather than sending it as an empty string.

dialog.runVerb.booleanPlaceholder.context: Placeholder of the two-item quick pick for a boolean (marker) argument. {argument} is the argument's own untranslated name.

dialog.runVerb.booleanYes.context: Label of the affirmative item in a boolean argument's quick pick. Choosing it sends the argument as true.

dialog.runVerb.booleanNo.context: Label of the negative item in a boolean argument's quick pick. Choosing it leaves the argument out of the call.

dialog.runVerb.vocabularyPlaceholder.context: Placeholder of the quick pick resolving an argument whose values are a closed set, which is either a set fixed in the source or one dinah resolves when it runs. {argument} is the argument's own untranslated name.

dialog.runVerb.omitOptional.context: Label of the first row in the quick pick for an optional argument whose values are a closed set. Choosing it leaves the argument out of the call, which Escape cannot do, because Escape abandons the whole wizard. {argument} is the argument's own untranslated name.

dialog.runVerb.requiredListPrompt.text: {argument} (required, one or more of {values}, separated by commas)
dialog.runVerb.requiredListPrompt.context: Prompt of the input box for a required argument whose value is a comma-separated list drawn from a fixed set. {argument} is the argument's own untranslated name and {values} is that set, also untranslated.

dialog.runVerb.optionalListPrompt.text: {argument} (optional, one or more of {values}, separated by commas; leave blank to omit)
dialog.runVerb.optionalListPrompt.context: Prompt of the input box for an optional argument whose value is a comma-separated list drawn from a fixed set. A blank answer leaves the argument out of the call. {argument} and {values} are untranslated.

dialog.runVerb.durationPlaceholder.context: Prompt of the input box for a duration-typed argument. The answer is passed through unexamined and parsed by the CLI's own ParseDuration.

dialog.runVerb.enumerationFailed.toast.text: Could not list Dinah's commands. See the Dinah output channel for details.
dialog.runVerb.enumerationFailed.toast.context: Toast when building the verb catalog failed outright: the dinah mcp spawn did not start, or its tools/list response could not be parsed.

dialog.runVerb.enumerationFailed.channel.text: Command palette: could not list Dinah's commands. {detail}
dialog.runVerb.enumerationFailed.channel.context: Output channel line beside the toast above, carrying the full spawn or transport failure. {detail} is that failure.

dialog.runVerb.noRenderableVerbs.toast.text: Dinah reported no command this version of the extension can run. See the Dinah output channel for details.
dialog.runVerb.noRenderableVerbs.toast.context: Toast when tools/list parsed but held no verb this build can render, whether because tools itself came back empty or every entry was unrenderable under this build's classifier.

dialog.runVerb.noRenderableVerbs.channel.text: Command palette: no command this build can run. {detail}
dialog.runVerb.noRenderableVerbs.channel.context: Output channel line beside the noRenderableVerbs toast. The listing succeeded here and the rendering did not, which is why this line is not the enumerationFailed one. {detail} is what the build reported.

dialog.runVerb.vocabularyResolutionFaile.text: Could not list the choices for {argument}. See the Dinah output channel for details.
dialog.runVerb.vocabularyResolutionFaile.context: Toast when the second call resolving a runtime-vocabulary argument failed, so the wizard for this one verb invocation stops without running it. {argument} is the argument's own untranslated name.

dialog.runVerb.vocabularyResolutionFaile.text: Command palette: could not resolve {argument} for {verb}. {detail}
dialog.runVerb.vocabularyResolutionFaile.context: Output channel line beside the toast above, carrying the full failure. {argument} and {verb} are their own untranslated names, {detail} the refusal.
